title: Parents, students and teachers protest LAUSD charter school budget cuts
seoTitle: Los Angeles protest over charter school cuts

tea.why: Protesters oppose a $10 million grant cut to 42 LAUSD-affiliated charter schools, citing concerns over safety, staffing, and student support.
tea.want: The reversal of the $10 million budget cut to the supplemental Charter School Block Grant.
tea.changed: Nov 10: Families, students, and teachers held rallies at multiple campuses across Los Angeles to oppose the planned funding reduction.

summary: On November 10, 2026, parents, students, and teachers organized a day of action across various Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) campuses to protest a planned $10 million reduction in annual funding for 42 affiliated charter schools. Participants expressed concerns that the cuts, scheduled for the 2027–2028 school year, would lead to staff layoffs, reduced campus supervision, and the loss of essential programs. Organizers at Riverside Drive Charter School estimated that the cuts could impact a significant portion of their site budget and staffing. In response, LAUSD stated the cuts are necessary to address a $3.6 billion deficit caused by declining enrollment, rising costs, and the end of federal COVID-19 relief funds. The district argued the move aims to standardize funding across all schools.
demands: Reverse the $10 million charter school grant cut
Ensure continued campus safety and supervision
response: LAUSD stated the cuts are necessary to address a $3.6 billion deficit and to create funding consistency across the district, noting that the supplemental grant was historically provided only to a specific subset of schools.

updates.text: Parents, students, and teachers held rallies at multiple LAUSD campuses to protest the $10 million budget cut.
